questions.prompt: What is the relationship between OpenAPI and Swagger?
options: They are two names for the same tool
Swagger is the specification; OpenAPI is a UI that renders it
OpenAPI is the specification (the contract); Swagger is the set of tools built around it
OpenAPI is only for ASP.NET Core; Swagger is for every other language
questions.explanation: OpenAPI is the language-agnostic standard for describing HTTP APIs, formerly known as the Swagger Specification; Swagger UI, Editor and Codegen are tools that work with it.

questions.prompt: Why is a single OpenAPI document useful to both backend and frontend teams?
options: It can generate documentation, client SDKs, server stubs and tests from one contract
It replaces the need for an HTTP server
It stores the API's database schema
It encrypts requests between frontend and backend
questions.explanation: Because the document describes endpoints, parameters, responses and auth in a standard format, the same file can drive docs, SDKs, stubs and tests and keep both sides aligned.

questions.prompt: In the example OpenAPI document, the `id` parameter of `/products/{id}` has `in: path` and `required: true`. What does that describe?
options: A value sent in the JSON request body
A mandatory part of the URL path, typed as an integer
questions.explanation: `in: path` places the parameter in the URL (`/products/{id}`), `required: true` makes it mandatory, and its schema says it is an `integer`.

questions.prompt: When does the lesson suggest using Swagger UI?
options: As a browser-based documentation page where developers can try endpoints manually, especially during development and for internal APIs
To replace authentication on public APIs
Only to write OpenAPI specs by hand
questions.explanation: Swagger UI renders interactive docs in the browser from an OpenAPI file, so developers can see how the API works and call endpoints by hand. Writing specs is Swagger Editor's job.
